chunks: Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, that he said:

Regarding a woman who menstruates once every three months or once every year, the mustaḥāḍah, the one who has not yet reached puberty, the one who menstruates once and then her menstruation stops once, the one who does not hope for a child, the one whose menstruation has ceased and claims that she has not despaired, and the one who sees yellow discharge from irregular menstruation, he mentioned that the waiting period of all of these women is three months.

key_terms.الصُّفْرَةَ: Yellowish discharge; here referring to abnormal or unclear menstrual-related discharge.
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةِ: A woman experiencing istiḥāḍah, meaning continuous or irregular non-menstrual bleeding.
key_terms.الْوَلَدِ: Child; in context, bearing children or hope of fertility.
key_terms.تَحِيضُ: She menstruates; used here to describe women with infrequent menstrual cycles.
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةُ أَشْهُرٍ: Three months; the specified legal duration of the waiting period in these cases.
key_terms.حَيْضُهَا: Her menstruation; refers to the woman’s menstrual cycle or bleeding.
key_terms.عِدَّةَ: The waiting period a divorced or widowed woman must observe before remarriage.

ai.seo_question: What is the ‘iddah of a woman with irregular, infrequent, or ceased menstruation in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the ‘iddah of several categories of women whose menstruation is absent, irregular, infrequent, or unclear. It establishes that the waiting period for all of these cases is three months, making it a jurisprudential text in family law.
